subject: Meteorology
title: Supercell Types
description: A micro-lesson that makes Supercell Types usable.

hook.text: Not all supercells look the same—three subtypes exist depending on moisture, shear, and storm environment.

buildup.text: Classic supercells have clear structure: a rotating updraft, distinct anvil, and visible wall cloud.

discovery.text: HP (high-precipitation) supercells wrap rain around the mesocyclone—hiding the tornado behind heavy downpours.

twist.text: LP (low-precipitation) supercells produce little rain, making their rotation easy to see—but hail can be extreme.

climax.text: HP supercells are the most dangerous to chasers—tornadoes hidden in rain give almost no visual warning.

punchline.text: The storm you can't see through may be the most dangerous.

quiz.question: Why are HP supercells particularly dangerous?
options: Rain hides the tornado from view
